_comment: #635. A row here does NOT excuse a ring — it names the surface that ring is actually painted on, and the guard measures the ratio against that surface instead of against the three theme tokens. `count` is per distinct utility per file, because the same utility can appear twice in one file on two different surfaces: TocReview shipped two `border-white` rings, one on `disabled:bg-green-800` (7.13) and one on `disabled:bg-muted` (1.09), and a file-level row would have pre-authorised the broken one. Shrink freely; delete the row when the ring goes.

src/components/toc/TocReview.tsx :: bord.reason: The accept button is a raw <button> whose `disabled:bg-green-800` paints at spinner time (`disabled` and the spinner share the `isLoading` flag). White on green-800 is 7.13:1. Surface-agnostic it would fail, because white on light `--muted` is 1.09 — which was exactly the sibling regenerate button's bug, fixed in this PR.

src/components/toc/ClarifyingQuestions.t.reason: Same shape as TocReview's accept button: raw <button>, `disabled:bg-green-800` at spinner time, 7.13:1.

src/components/BookCreationWizard.tsx.reason: The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. Explicit `bg-primary text-primary-foreground` on the submit button.

src/components/books/DeleteBookModal.tsx.reason: The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. `variant="destructive"` is `bg-destructive text-white`.

src/components/chapters/questions/Questi.reason: The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. `variant="outline"` keeps `bg-background` and the inherited `--foreground`.

The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. The regenerate control is `variant="ghost"`, which paints no background of its own, so the icon sits on the page surface in the inherited `--foreground`. (The other spinner in this file declares `text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400` and is swept normally.)

A `◌` glyph, not a ring, in a default <Button> (`bg-primary text-primary-foreground`). As a text character its obligation is 1.4.3, not 1.4.11; it is measured here at the 3:1 floor alongside the rings rather than left out. Note the button is disabled while it spins, so `disabled:opacity-50` from button.tsx's base halves the real contrast for this and every other disabled button in the app — tracked separately, not a spinner bug.

src/components/chapters/questions/Regene.reason: The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. Default variant on the confirm button.

src/components/examples/ai-error-handlin.reason: The icon is `currentColor` inside a <Button>, so it paints the button's own foreground on the button's own background — a pair shadcn defines together in `button.tsx`, not a colour that lands on a page surface. Three default-variant buttons in the same demo component.

src/components/chapters/ChapterEditor.ts.reason: The save-status spinner is `currentColor` inside a `text-xs text-muted-foreground` span. This is the site that showed why colourless spinners need rows at all: with no utility of its own it produced no sweep entry, so this guard's own "every ring" claim was false for it until review caught it.

src/components/ui/sonner.tsx.reason: Sonner's `icons.loading`. The toast root sets `--normal-bg: var(--popover)` and `--normal-text: var(--popover-foreground)`, so the icon paints that pair rather than anything on the page behind it.
